Project Title: DAKOR WATER SUPPLY PROJECT
IRMA Major Observations: The quality of work for the sump at the WTP main head works was found to be substandard. Slurry loss was observed in several areas, and the shuttering line level was inadequate. Exposed steel bars were found in the slab at multiple locations, and the column-slab joints were not properly formed. The steel of the staircase was also exposed due to improper shuttering, and the required concrete cover was not provided. Additionally, no shuttering inspection was conducted by the concerned staff prior to concreting. Major honeycombing was observed in several areas, and the shuttering plates were not removed properly after concreting. It is strongly recommended to maintain a concrete pour card record for each level inspection to prevent the recurrence of these issues. This reflects significant negligence on the part of the concerned PMC/ULB staff. The quality of work is unacceptable, and a detailed structural verification, along with supporting test reports, must be submitted for approval before proceeding further.

Project Title: Renovation of Greater Mamit Water Supply Scheme.
IRMA Major Observations: During our recent site visit, it was noted that the rising main MS pipes lack exterior painting and do not have an internal lining. This absence of inside lining raises significant concerns regarding the longevity of the pipes and the quality of the water being transported. Additionally, without proper exterior painting, the MS pipes are at an increased risk of corrosion over time, which could lead to further complications and potential failures in the system. It is imperative to address these issues promptly to ensure the durability and effectiveness of the installation.

Project Title: Renovation of Greater Mamit Water Supply Scheme.
IRMA Major Observations: During site visit, a proper alignment drawing for the rising main pipeline was not available. These vital documents should have reflected essential information, including the road and street names, pipe diameters, node to node distances, flow directions, valve positions, thrust block/RCC concrete block locations, depth of the pipe top from NGL, and the gradient of the pipes. The absence of these detailed alignments impeded a thorough assessment and understanding of the project scope, underscoring the necessity for proper documentation to ensure efficient project execution moving forward.

Project Title: Renovation of Greater Mamit Water Supply Scheme.
IRMA Major Observations: The absence of an RCC thrust block or anchor block for the rising main pipeline is a significant concern that must be addressed to ensure the stability and integrity of the system. Without these critical supports, the pipeline may experience excessive movement or shifting, potentially leading to damage or failure.

Project Title: Renovation of Greater Mamit Water Supply Scheme.
IRMA Major Observations: Rate considered in rate analysis for welding in 219 mm diameter MS pipe is Rs. 19082.08 per joint. The rate proposed for the project may require revision based on several observations outlined below. Firstly, certain items included in the rate analysis, such as welding glass, chipping hammers, steel brushes, electrode holders, welding cables, and welding machines, are tools that can be reused multiple times. It is crucial to consider their cost-effectiveness in the overall analysis. Secondly, the manpower allocation for each welding joint appears to be excessive; the analysis lists 1 welder, 1 grinder, 1 engine operator, 2 fitters, and 4 helpers, which is not appropriate for a single welding joint. Lastly, the cost attributed to the 4 mm diameter electrode, set at RS 2000.00 each, seems unreasonably high and should be reassessed. We need to address these points to ensure a fair and accurate pricing structure for this project.

Reinforcement bars were not aligned perpendicular to the wall as required. 3. This misalignment may affect structural integrity. 4. No PMC (Project Management Consultant) representative was present during the concreting activity, which is a deviation from standard supervision protocols. 5. The construction joint was poorly executed, potentially leading to weak bonding and leakage issues. 7. Foundation and RE wall reinforcement connection with previously casted structure was not done nor expansion joint provided. As per above comment foundation concrete work was not acceptable need to recast and supporting photo must be attached. Also, action should be taken on PMC for this major negligence to minimize such mistake in feature.

Furthermore, it was noted that key joints or water stoppers were not provided during construction, which is critical for water-retaining structures. Project Title: AMRUT 2.0 : WATER SUPPLY WARD NO -12 DISTRIBUTION NETWORK
IRMA Major Observations: DI pipe laying work is currently in progress. During the site visit, it was observed that the riding main and distribution lines are connected at several locations without the provision of valves. This compromises the intended functionality of the riding main system, as both pipelines are laid in parallel and directly interconnected. The riding main was designed to minimize leakage and maintain adequate pressure up to the end point; however, multiple unvalved connections defeat this purpose and may lead to pressure loss and uncontrolled flow. It is recommended to review the design and revise the execution plan to ensure proper utilization and functionality of the laid pipeline network.

Evidence such as droppings, feathers, twigs, and nesting materials was observed scattered across the ESR floor. The extent of contamination made it difficult and unsafe to access the facility. - Bird droppings can severely compromise drinking water quality by introducing harmful microorganisms, including E. coli, Salmonella, and Cryptosporidium. This presents a significant public health risk and could lead to outbreaks of waterborne diseases. - Immediate Actions Required: Seal all potential entry points to prevent further access by birds. Perform a thorough cleaning and disinfection of the ESR. Conduct comprehensive water quality testing to ensure compliance with drinking water standards before resuming supply. Implement all necessary corrective measures without delay.

IRMA Major Observations: Despite repeated comments and instructions to the agency during previous visits, the rectification work on the Santrampur ESR dome and leakage issues remains incomplete. The agency informed that leakage treatment had been carried out; however, seepage is still observed on-site, indicating ineffective rectification. Additionally, honeycombing and exposed reinforcement bars are still present in several areas of the dome and require immediate repair. The ESR dome manhole cutout also needs proper finishing. Although the ventilation opening has been covered with an MS mosquito mesh, for better durability and long-term performance, it is recommended to install an MS grill or GI mesh instead. During this visit, it is clearly instructed that all pending rectifications must be completed without further delay. PMC monitoring should be strengthened, and necessary action must be taken by the ULB to ensure compliance and quality of work.

The thrust block must extend at least 300 mm beyond the opening in all six directions to ensure the structural integrity of the ESR. Additionally, please provide before and after photographs of the thrust block installation for documentation.

Project Title: GODHRA LAXMANSAGAR WATER BODY REJUVENATION
Category: Variation in Scope of Work & Cost
IRMA Major Observations: The toe beam design for the project was revised from the original tender specifications to incorporate a pile foundation. However, this revision was not approved by the concern authority prior to commencement of the work, as required. Additionally, a 150 mm PCC layer was considered beneath the stone pitching as an extra item without obtaining prior approval. It is important to note that the provision of PCC below the pitching is not viable, as it obstructs the natural mechanism for releasing earth pressure. Furthermore, laying uniform-sized stones over the PCC is impractical, which would result in a reduction in stone size and ultimately weaken the overall pitching structure.

Miyawaki Plantation: The base layers and plant species used in the Miyawaki plantation were not as per the tender requirements. 5. PA System and Lighting: All components of the PA system and lighting work need to be thoroughly verified, as several items, including the TV, were not observed on site. 6. Ornamental Grill: The tender specified ornamental grills, but regular fabricated grills were installed at the site. 7. Pile Work Below Compound Wall: Pile work was carried out below the compound wall without prior approval or reference to approved drawings. Any such extra items must be formally approved before processing for payment, and must be supported by photographic evidence and relevant approved drawings. It must be ensured that payment is made only for items that have been executed as per site conditions and tender specifications.

Project Title: AMRUT 2.0: RENOVATION AND RECONSTRUCTION OF DRAINAGE NETWORK OF OLD VALSAD CITY
IRMA Major Observations: - Land clearance for the Garib Nawaz Pumping Station was received in March-25, and the civil works were completed in June-25. This is a critical pumping station because, due to its non-operation, sewerage from three other pumping stations is being disposed of openly. This is a serious issue, and the GPCB has issued several reminders to stop the open discharge of untreated sewerage. - Despite the critical nature of this issue and repeated priority requests from the Nagarpalika to GUDC, the pumping station has not yet been commissioned. Although the civil works were completed six months ago, the station could not be started due to pending approval of the electro-mechanical components. - Based on site discussions, it is observed that the major delay is due to delayed drawing and material approvals from the PMC. Upon reviewing the PMC’s drawing approval mechanism, it appears impractical. The PMC first asks for civil structure drawings, followed by QAP approvals in parts (pump QAP, then panel QAP, factory visit approvals, and other stages). - As per previous records, drawing approval for the pump QAP alone takes an average of 2 to 3 months, and a similar time is required for panel QAP approvals and subsequent stages. This sequential approval process is causing significant delays. - Based on the above observations, it is clear that the current drawing approval mechanism is impractical. The contractor should be instructed to submit all relevant drawings and QAPs together, and the PMC should issue consolidated observations at one time to avoid repeated rejections and unnecessary loss of time. This was observed in many projects of GUDC. - The PMC has been appointed to ensure timely project completion with quality work. However, no significant positive measures taken by the PMC to improve project progress have been observed. If any such measures have been taken, details along with supporting documents should be provided. - Further, all reasons for the delays should be clearly explained with supporting documents and proper justification, including identification of responsibility for the delay and the resulting avoidable pollution.

Project Title: AMRELI ROKADIYA LAKE DEVELOPMENT
IRMA Major Observations: Based on the approved DPR, the following improvements are required to enhance project utilization, structural performance, and long-term durability: 1. The PCC proposed below the pitching is not suitable for effective earth pressure release. Furthermore, the pitching stones are of random sizes, resulting in improper leveling and inadequate interlocking. This requires immediate review and correction. 2. PCC blocks of size 0.75 m × 0.70 m proposed below the toe beam represent a substantial and unjustified concrete volume. Instead, piles may be considered up to the hard rock level. If hard rock is encountered at a depth of less than 1.0 m, an RE wall would be a more appropriate and economical solution. This design shall be reviewed and necessary improvements implemented accordingly. 3. Solar lights are currently proposed; however, their functionality cannot be ensured throughout the year due to cleaning and weather-related issues. It is recommended to consider independent solar panels mounted on the toilet block and other suitable locations around the water body to ensure reliable power supply. This aspect shall be reviewed and revised as required. 4. Pitching on both faces of the embankment should be considered. If feasible, the roadside face of the embankment may be developed by providing a beam grid on the slope, with alternate panels stabilized using scrub-type small flowering plants for long-term slope protection and aesthetic improvement.

Project Title: AMRUT 2.0: TRANCH-3: Providing and laying water supply Distribution line and pumping machinery at various location of Jambusar Nagarpalika.
IRMA Major Observations: The higher zone sump slab work has been completed. However, the quality of the RCC slab is found to be poor, with honeycombing observed at multiple locations and reinforcement exposed near the opening areas. Despite prior instructions for quality improvement, no satisfactory improvement has been observed. As the sump slab is directly exposed to chlorine gas, any honeycombing will significantly reduce the service life of the slab. Therefore, it is mandatory to remove all loose aggregates and rectify the honeycombed areas by filling them with approved micro-concrete. In addition, a proper waterproof plaster treatment shall be applied to the entire bottom surface of the sump slab to minimize the impact on its durability and service life.

Project Title: AMRUT 2.0: TRANCH-3: Providing and laying water supply Distribution line and pumping machinery at various location of Jambusar Nagarpalika.
IRMA Major Observations: As per the instructions given during 8th Sep-25 visit, RCC staircases for both inside and outside the sump, along with a staircase cabin and SS railing, were required to be provided. However, the PMC did not incorporate this requirement during the design approval stage, and the same has not been executed at site. As evident from the attached photographs, the tender item description clearly specifies the provision of an RCC staircase with SS railing and a staircase cabin. Despite this, the tender specifications were not considered during drawing approval and execution. In view of the above, please provide detailed reasons for not adhering to the tender specifications during the design approval process. Additionally, submit the proposed remedial measures to incorporate the RCC staircase with SS railing and staircase cabin as per tender provisions.

Project Title: AMRUT 2.0: TRANCH-3: Providing and laying water supply Distribution line and pumping machinery at various location of Jambusar Nagarpalika.

The contractor is advised to immediately provide proper end caps on all HSC pipes as per standard practice until the final connection is completed .

The contractor is advised to remove the improperly laid tiles, compact the base layers properly, and re-install the tiles with correct interlocking and proper level to ensure durable and standard road restoration.
